assertions.name: atom_convex_2cable_also_clears_the_requirement
assertions.source: sum_b w_b tr_M(2-cable of beta_b) / sqrt(B_AME), the framework's own branch weights -- not the max over branches

description: The 2-parallel cable of the deuteron braid -- a genuine satellite -- reaches max_b tr_M = 7.448220 against the required 1.491498, i.e. 4.99x over, where the uncabled word reached only 1.018275 (0.683x). The atom's OWN convex-weighted 2-cable also clears it, at 1.657034 = 1.111x -- a thin margin. The satellite escapes the branch-convexity bound exactly as QOU.MassTheory.larger_index_set_escapes_the_bound predicted. Does NOT reproduce binding: the cost, support, Gram and LP all change at n=12 and none of that is redone; exceeding a NECESSARY condition is not sufficiency.
caveats: Scope (a). This does NOT reproduce binding. The cost vector, support, Gram and the whole LP change at n = 12 and none of it is redone here; exceeding a NECESSARY condition (a concentrated cost needs tr_M >= sqrt(B_AME)) is not sufficiency, and nothing here computes a binding contribution.

The pattern is a CHOICE. 2-parallel with blackboard framing is one satellite among infinitely many; nothing derives it, and a different pattern gives different numbers. And Geom still assigns nothing to a satellite -- this shows the room exists, not that the framework can use it.

A longer word generally has a larger trace, so 'the cable is bigger' is not by itself interesting. What is: the geometrically-motivated move crosses the threshold by 5x rather than marginally, and the Lean predicted this class escapes before the number was computed.

block_rep_braid_word returns float64, so this is float64; the verdict turns on a factor of 5. The first attempt used per_block_evaluation, which builds all 77 partitions of 12 and reached 9.99 GB RSS before being killed; restricting to the 7 two-row blocks that matter under convention D ran the whole sweep in 3.6 s.
